title: Evidence-Based Team Sizing and Composition
purpose: Defines optimal team sizes and compositions based on empirical data from 28 team sessions with 132 agent instances. Prevents the recurring pattern of over-sized teams that lose 89% per-agent efficiency.

section_1_sizing_rules.title: Team Sizing Rules
section_1_sizing_rules.description: Hard rules derived from empirical data. Violating these requires explicit justification.

rules.rule: Solo agent (1) for independent research tasks
rules.evidence: T05: 4.0 artifacts/agent — highest efficiency ever recorded. T10-T13: each solo agent produced complete API catalogs.

rules.rule: Small team (3) for focused tool building
rules.evidence: T06: 1.0 artifacts/agent — 3 agents built 3 tools with no wasted effort.
when_to_use: Implementing a single feature with tests
Writing SOPs for a specific subsystem

rules.evidence: T27: 5 agents, full repo audit in 90 seconds, zero idle time. T24: 8 agents, stress tests + SOPs. T02: 7 agents, complete research API.

recommended_composition.7_agent: 1 coordinator + 2 think tanks + 2 coding teams + 1 research + 1 standby
recommended_composition.8_agent: 1 coordinator + 2 think tanks + 3 coding teams + 1 research + 1 standby

rules.rule: Large team (9-12) for research operations ONLY
rules.evidence: T07: 9 agents (3 leads x 2 subs) optimal for research with parallel streams. T14: 9 agents for API tool building.
when_to_use: Competitive analysis with multiple independent evaluations
rules.required_structure: Must use lead-sub pattern (1 lead per 2-3 sub-agents)

rules.rule: AVOID teams of 15+ agents unless unique capability required
rules.evidence: T03 (27 agents): 0.44 artifacts/agent, 89% efficiency loss. T09 (20 agents): 0.45 artifacts/agent. T25 (15 agents): required user correction for sequential patterns.
rules.when_to_use: ONLY when the task requires one of these unique multi-team capabilities that cannot be achieved with smaller teams:
unique_capabilities: Competitive verification (independent quality scoring of same target)
Cross-team bug detection (bugs found via inter-team friction)
Parallel multi-language implementation (e.g., Python + Go simultaneously)
rules.required_justification: Coordinator must document which unique capability justifies the size before launching

section_2_composition_patterns.title: Standard Team Compositions
section_2_composition_patterns.description: Pre-validated team compositions for common operation types.

patterns.name: Bug Hunt
patterns.evidence: T25 found 14 bugs at 0.93/agent with this pattern
patterns.workflow: Think tanks find -> coding teams fix -> think tanks verify

patterns.name: Feature Build
patterns.evidence: T02 pattern: think tank designs, research provides context, coding implements
patterns.workflow: Research + think tank in parallel -> coding teams implement -> standby helps stragglers

patterns.name: Audit & Analysis
patterns.evidence: T27: full repo audit in 90s with this pattern
patterns.workflow: Audit teams scan in parallel -> think tank synthesizes findings

patterns.name: Data Pipeline
patterns.evidence: Derived from TT-OBS-1 recommendations (1 sorter per 2 gatherers)
patterns.workflow: Gatherers produce -> sorters categorize -> think tank spot-checks quality

patterns.name: Market Research Sprint
patterns.evidence: Extrapolated from T03 competitive research pattern, right-sized per SIZE-03
patterns.workflow: Research teams gather independently -> analysis cross-validates -> coding builds tools if needed

section_3_decision_flowchart.title: Team Size Decision Flowchart
steps: 1. Is this a single research question or code fix? → Solo (SIZE-01)
2. Is this building 2-4 related deliverables? → Small team of 3 (SIZE-02)
3. Does this need parallel streams with integration? → Medium team of 5-8 (SIZE-03)
4. Does this need 3+ independent research domains? → Large team of 9-12 (SIZE-04)
5. Does this require a unique multi-team capability? → 15+ with written justification (SIZE-05)
6. If unsure: start with 5 agents. Add more only if blocked.

patterns.symptom: Launching 15+ agents for tasks achievable by 5-7
patterns.evidence: T03 (27 agents), T09 (20 agents) both achieved < 0.5 artifacts/agent
patterns.fix: Start with SIZE-03 (5-8). Only scale up with evidence of need.

patterns.symptom: Assigning one agent to each source file for modification
patterns.evidence: Causes resource conflicts (SOP-012 TRIG-07). Better to assign by subsystem.
patterns.fix: Group related files under one agent. Use subsystem boundaries, not file boundaries.

patterns.symptom: More think tanks than coding teams
patterns.evidence: T21 had 3 think tanks + 1 coordinator analyzing Proto A; could have been 1 think tank + data
patterns.fix: Maximum ratio: 1 think tank per 2 coding teams. Think tanks produce plans; coding teams produce artifacts.

patterns.symptom: All agents assigned critical work; no slack for redistribution
patterns.evidence: T27 zero idle time came from pre-loaded work queue, not from having zero slack
patterns.fix: For teams of 7+, include 1 standby agent or pre-load WorkStealing queue with fallback tasks

before_launch: Team size matches task complexity per SIZE-01 through SIZE-05
If 15+ agents: written justification for unique capability requirement
Composition follows a validated pattern from section 2 (or documented deviation)
Think tank to coding team ratio is ≤ 1:2
Standby agent or pre-loaded work queue for teams of 7+
